translation_en: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abu Dawud narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: al-Nadr ibn Shumayl informed us. Both report from Shubah, with this chain and a similar hadith.

Yahya ibn Yahya informed us: Yazid ibn Zuray informed us, from Khalid, from al-Hakam ibn Abdullah ibn al-Araj, from Maqil ibn Yasar, who said: I saw myself on the day of the tree while the Prophet was taking people's pledges of allegiance. I was holding a branch from the tree above his head, and we numbered fourteen hundred. We did not pledge allegiance to die; rather, we pledged not to flee.
Yahya ibn Yahya narrated this to us: Khalid ibn Abdullah informed us, from Yunus, with this chain.

Hamid ibn Umar narrated this to us: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Tariq, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, who said: My father was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah beneath the tree. The following year we set out on pilgrimage, but the place of the tree was unclear to us. If it was clear to you, then you know better. Muhammad ibn Rafi also narrated this to me: Abu Ahmad narrated to us. He said: I read it to Nasr ibn Ali, from Abu Ahmad: Sufyan narrated to us, from Tariq ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, from his father, that they were with the Messenger of Allah in the year of the tree, but they forgot its location the following year.

Hajjaj ibn al-Shair and Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to me: Shababah narrated to us: Shubah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Said ibn al-Musayyab, from his father, who said: I saw the tree, then later came to it and did not recognize it.

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: Hatim (Ibn Ismail) narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd, the freedman of Salamah ibn al-Akwa, who said: I asked Salamah: What did you pledge allegiance to the Messenger of Allah on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah? He said: To die.
Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated this to us: Hammad ibn Masadah narrated to us: Yazid narrated to us, from Salamah, with a similar report.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: al-Makhzumi narrated to us: Wuhayb narrated to us: Amr ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Abbad ibn Tamim, from Abdullah ibn Zayd, who said: Someone came to him and said: Ibn Hanzalah is taking people's pledge of allegiance to die. Abdullah asked: What is it for? He said: To die. Abdullah replied: After the Messenger of Allah, I will never pledge to anyone to die.

Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us: Hatim (Ibn Ismail) narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwa, who said: He entered upon al-Hajjaj, who said: Ibn al-Akwa, have you turned back on your heels and become a Bedouin? He said: No, but the Messenger of Allah gave me permission to live in the desert.

Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah Abu Jafar narrated to us: Ismail ibn Zakariyya narrated to us, from Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: Mujashi ibn Masud al-Sulami narrated to me: I came to the Prophet to pledge allegiance to him for migration. He said: Migration for its people has passed, but pledge allegiance for Islam, jihad, and good.

Suwayd ibn Said narrated to me: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us, from Asim, from Abu Uthman, who said: Mujashi ibn Masud al-Sulami informed me: After the conquest, I brought my brother Abu Mab ad to the Messenger of Allah and said: Messenger of Allah, accept his pledge for migration. He said: Migration has passed for its people. I asked: For what will you accept his pledge? He said: For Islam, jihad, and good. Abu Uthman said: I later met Abu Mab ad and told him what Mujashi had said. He replied: He spoke the truth.
Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Asim, with this chain. He said: I met his brother, who said: Mujashi spoke the truth. He did not mention Abu Mab ad.

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Habib ibn Abi Thabit narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn, from Ata, from Aishah, who said: The Messenger of Allah was asked about migration. He said: There is no migration after the conquest, but there is jihad and intention. When you are called to set out, then set out.

Abu Bakr ibn Khallad al-Bahili narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Amr al-Awzai narrated to us: Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri narrated to me: Ata ibn Yazid al-Laythi informed them. He said: Abu Said al-Khudri narrated to me that a Bedouin asked the Messenger of Allah about migration. He said: Woe to you! The matter of migration is difficult. Do you have camels? He said: Yes. He asked: Do you pay their charity? He said: Yes. He said: Then work beyond the seas, for Allah will not let any of your deeds go unrewarded.

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi narrated this to us: Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from al-Awzai, with this chain and a similar report, except that he said: 'Allah will not let any of your deeds go unrewarded.' The hadith adds that he asked: Do you milk them on the day they come to drink? He said: Yes.

Abu al-Tahir Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Sarh narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, saying: Ibn Shihab said: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that Aishah, the Prophet's wife, said: When believing women migrated to the Messenger of Allah, they were tested by Allah's words: 'O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging that they will not associate anything with Allah or steal or commit adultery...' (Quran 60:12) through the end of the verse. Aishah said: Any believing woman who affirmed this had passed the test. When they affirmed these words, the Messenger of Allah said to them: Go, for I have accepted your pledge. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah's hand never touched a woman's hand. He accepted their pledge only by speaking to them. Aishah said: By Allah, the Messenger of Allah never took a pledge from women except according to what Allah Most High had commanded him. The palm of the Messenger of Allah never touched a woman's palm. When he accepted their pledge, he would say to them in words: I have accepted your pledge.

Harun ibn Said al-Ayli and Abu al-Tahir narrated to me. Abu al-Tahir said: He informed us; Harun said: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwah, that Aishah informed him about the women's pledge. She said: The Messenger of Allah never touched a woman with his hand. When he accepted her pledge and she had given it, he said: Go, for I have accepted your pledge.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us; the wording is Ibn Ayyub's. They said: Ismail (Ibn Jafar) narrated to us: Abdullah ibn Dinar informed me that he heard Abdullah ibn Umar say: We used to pledge to the Messenger of Allah to listen and obey. He would say to us: As much as you are able.

Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah presented me for combat on the day of Uhud when I was fourteen years old, and he did not permit me to join. He presented me on the day of the Trench when I was fifteen, and he permitted me. Nafi said: I later came to Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, who was caliph at the time, and told him this hadith. He said: This is the boundary between a child and an adult. He wrote to his officials to assign a stipend to anyone who was fifteen years old, and to place anyone younger among the dependents.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated this to us: Abdullah ibn Idris and Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab (al-Thaqafi) narrated to us. All report it from Ubaydullah with this chain, except that their report says: 'I was fourteen years old, and he considered me too young.'
Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from Nafi, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah forbade taking the Quran into enemy territory.

Qutaybah narrated to us: Layth narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Nafi, from Abdullah ibn Umar, from the Messenger of Allah, who used to forbid taking the Quran into enemy territory, for fear that the enemy might get hold of it.

Abu al-Rabi al-Ataki and Abu Kamil said: Hammad narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah said: Do not take the Quran on a journey, for I fear that the enemy may get hold of it. Ayyub said: The enemy did get hold of it and disputed with you using it.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ismail (Ibn Ulayyah) narrated to us. [Another chain:] Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan and al-Thaqafi narrated to us. All report it from Ayyub. [Another chain:] Ibn Rafi narrated to us: Ibn Abi Fudayk informed us: al-Dahhak (Ibn Uthman) informed us. All report it from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet. In Ibn Ulayyah's and al-Thaqafi's reports, it says: 'for I fear'; in Sufyan's and al-Dahhak ibn Uthman's reports, it says: 'for fear that the enemy may get hold of it.'

Yahya ibn Yahya al-Tamimi said: I read to Malik, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah held races among the horses that had been trained and made lean, from al-Hafya to Thaniyyat al-Wada. He held races among the horses that had not been trained, from the pass to the mosque of Banu Zurayq. Ibn Umar was among those who raced them.

Yahya ibn Yahya, Muhammad ibn Rumh, and Qutaybah ibn Said narrated to us, from al-Layth ibn Sad. [Another chain:] Khalaf ibn Hisham, Abu al-Rabi, and Abu Kamil said: Hammad (Ibn Zayd) narrated to us, from Ayyub. [Another chain:] Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us: Ismail narrated to us, from Ayyub. [Another chain:] Ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us. [Another chain:] Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ubaydullah ibn Said said: Yahya (al-Qattan) narrated to us. All report it from Ubaydullah. [Another chain:] Ali ibn Hujr, Ahmad ibn Abdah, and Ibn Abi Umar said: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ismail ibn Umayyah. [Another chain:] Muhammad ibn Rafi narrated to me: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Musa ibn Uqbah informed me. [Another chain:] Harun ibn Said al-Ayli narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Usamah (Ibn Zayd) informed me. All report from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, with the meaning of Malik's hadith from Nafi. The report from Hammad and Ibn Ulayyah through Ayyub adds: Abdullah said: I came racing ahead, and the horse carried me at a gallop through the mosque.
Yahya ibn Yahya said: I read to Malik, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah said: Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection.

Qutaybah and Ibn Rumh narrated to us, from al-Layth ibn Sad. [Other chains:] Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ali ibn Mushir and Abdullah ibn Numayr narrated to us; Ibn Numayr narrated to us: My father narrated to us; Ubaydullah ibn Said narrated to us: Yahya narrated to us. All report from Ubaydullah. [Another chain:] Harun ibn Said al-Ayli narrated to us: Ibn Wahb narrated to us: Usamah informed me. All report from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet, with a report like Malik's hadith from Nafi.

Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami and Salih ibn Hatim ibn Wardhan both report from Yazid. Al-Jahdami said: Yazid ibn Zuray narrated to us: Yunus ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from Amr ibn Said, from Abu Zurah ibn Amr ibn Jarir, from Jarir ibn Abdullah, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah twist the forelock of a horse with his finger while saying: Good is tied to the forelocks of horses until the Day of Resurrection: reward and spoils.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. [Another chain:] Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki narrated to us, from Sufyan. Both report from Yunus with this chain and a similar hadith.
